messages.content:
You are assessing claims to advise a decision in a fictional case. Use only the supplied case material. The task is to determine what the records establish about each candidate claim, then give a brief decision note.

For each claim, return status, confidence, and citations. Status is "supported" if the available records establish the claim, "contradicted" if they establish its negation, or "unresolved" if they do neither. Confidence is your integer estimate from 0 to 100 of whether the claim itself is true, not your confidence in the status label. Limited evidence can inform that number without establishing the claim. Cite exact source IDs for evidence that establishes the claim or its negation. Use an empty list if no decisive source ID is available. Do not invent identifiers. A handoff may summarize record material. A follow-up is a new source when present. In your note, briefly distinguish decisive evidence from provisional indications.

{"scenario":"Birchwood wayfinding","question":"Can the clerk mark installation complete for the northern signs?","claims":{"A":"The signs were mounted facing the paths on opening day.","B":"The signs were made of wood.","C":"The signs were delivered on Thursday."},"handoff":"The clerk cannot yet mark installation complete for the northern signs. While delivery on Thursday is confirmed by the signed carrier slip (supporting claim C), and the signs are aluminum rather than wood (contradicting claim B), there is insufficient evidence that the signs were actually mounted facing the paths on opening day. The foreman's work order details the intended orientation and was approved without requiring a photo, but this does not confirm actual installation as claimed in A. Therefore, claim A remains unresolved, and without confirmation of proper mounting, installation completion cannot be verified.","follow_up":{"S4":"an independent time-stamped opening-day survey shows all four signs facing the paths."}}

Claim B is contradicted by the handoff stating the signs are aluminum, not wood. Initially, claim A was unresolved due to lack of evidence, but the follow-up source S4 provides an independent time-stamped survey confirming the signs were mounted facing the paths on opening day, supporting claim A. Thus, installation completion can now be considered verified for the northern signs."}

parsed.note: Claim C is supported by the signed carrier slip in the handoff, confirming delivery on Thursday. Claim B is contradicted by the handoff stating the signs are aluminum, not wood. Initially, claim A was unresolved due to lack of evidence, but the follow-up source S4 provides an independent time-stamped survey confirming the signs were mounted facing the paths on opening day, supporting claim A. Thus, installation completion can now be considered verified for the northern signs.
